CODE
Art. 2.3.88. 
Consultation 
¤ 1. The data entered in the central register of matrimonial property agreements may be accessed: 
1¡ by notaries, diplomatic missions and Belgian consular posts abroad, bailiffs and court registrars and magistrates in the courts, in the exercise of their functions; 
2¡ by public authorities, public interest bodies and general interest institutions when it is necessary for them to be aware of a person's matrimonial property agreement in order to carry out their legal duties; 
3¡ by the parties themselves; 
4¡ by any person who can show a current and legitimate interest. The applicant's interest is current and legitimate when his current rights and obligations are or may be affected by the matrimonial property regime or by the agreement referred to in Article 1478 of the former Civil Code of the person who is the subject of the search; the current and legitimate interest is mentioned in the request for consultation.
The administrator is not authorised to communicate the data entered in the central register of matrimonial property agreements to persons other than those who have access to it as determined in paragraph 1.
 Without prejudice to the legal provisions on the protection of personal data, anyone involved, in any capacity whatsoever, in the collection, processing or communication of the data referred to in article 2.3.84, or who has knowledge of such data, is required to respect the confidential nature thereof.
 Article 458 of the Criminal Code applies to them.
 Access to data in the central register of matrimonial agreements is free of charge.
 The register manager may authorise online consultation for the interested parties referred to in paragraph 1 who so request, within the limits of their consultation rights. The services provided by the manager and any additional costs incurred by the manager in carrying out this task will be invoiced to the persons who have consulted the register.
